summary: Indignation can show in a face or find expression in a public denunciation. Balaam refuses Balak’s request to denounce Israel, since God has given him no such word. Psalm 7 speaks of the indignation of a righteous judge.

senses.gloss: indignation that breaks out in judgment
senses.definition: Nahum sets Yahweh’s indignation beside the burning of his anger. Isaiah says the people should take shelter for a little while until the indignation passes.
The psalm pairs God as a righteous judge with his daily indignation. Isaiah sets his indignation against his enemies beside his care for his servants.
Balak calls Balaam to denounce Israel. Balaam replies that he cannot denounce one whom Yahweh has not denounced. Nations denounce a judge who pronounces the wicked righteous.
Secret speech produces indignant looks, just as the north wind brings rain.

note: Arabic زَعَمَ in Lane p. 1232 is to assert or claim. That speech verb does not establish the specific meaning of angry denunciation. The proposed different comparison with تَزَغَّمَ lacks a verified own-language locator here. No assignment of the older sounds behind zayin and ayin rests on those comparisons.
